peptide.name: Melanotan II
peptide.summary: Melanotan II is a synthetic, non-selective melanocortin receptor agonist developed at the University of Arizona as a tanning agent. It activates MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, and MC5R with comparable affinity, producing skin pigmentation and, as an incidental finding in early trials, erectile/libido effects. It is not FDA-approved or approved by any regulatory agency for any use, and carries documented safety concerns distinct from its FDA-approved, more selective derivative bremelanotide (PT-141).
peptide.description: Melanotan II (Ac-Nle-cyclo[Asp-His-D-Phe-Arg-Trp-Lys]-NH2) is a cyclic heptapeptide analog of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH), originally developed as a potential skin-cancer-prevention strategy by inducing protective tanning without UV exposure. Unlike native alpha-MSH, which preferentially activates MC1R on melanocytes, MT-2 is non-selective and activates MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, and MC5R with broadly comparable affinity. This non-selectivity is clinically significant: MC4R activation in the hypothalamus and spinal cord drives the erectile/libido effect that emerged as an unanticipated finding in the first human pilot trials (and was later developed separately into the FDA-approved, more selective drug bremelanotide/PT-141), while MC3R/MC5R activation contributes to appetite suppression and other autonomic effects. No government regulatory agency has approved any MT-2-containing product. Documented human harms include a published case report of eruptive atypical nevi and growth of pre-existing nevi in a patient with prior melanoma and dysplastic nevus syndrome (Cardones & Grichnik, 2009), plus other published reports of priapism requiring surgical intervention and rhabdomyolysis associated with self-administered use.
peptide.mechanism_of_action: Non-selective agonist across the melanocortin receptor family (MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, MC5R). MC1R activation on melanocytes stimulates eumelanin synthesis (tanning). MC4R activation in the central nervous system drives sexual arousal/erectile activity and contributes to appetite suppression; MC3R/MC5R activation produces additional autonomic effects (cardiovascular tone, exocrine secretion).

half_life.note: Short half-life typical of small cyclic peptides; precise modern human pharmacokinetic data are limited given the compound was never approved for clinical use.

peptide.evidence_note: Small human pilot studies in the 1990s-2000s confirmed tanning and erectile effects, but also documented dose-limiting nausea and flushing, and the compound was not advanced to approval due to its non-selective receptor profile and safety findings. Its more selective successor, bremelanotide (PT-141), was developed instead and gained FDA approval for a specific indication. Published case reports document serious adverse events with self-administered MT-2 use, outside any regulated clinical trial setting.
peptide.fda_status_note: Not approved by the FDA or any regulatory agency for any indication. Distinct from the FDA-approved drug bremelanotide (PT-141/Vyleesi), a more selective, structurally related melanocortin agonist. Sold as a research chemical or through unregulated online/gray-market sources 'for research use only' or for cosmetic tanning, which does not constitute approved medical use.
peptide.compounding_note: Not an FDA-approved drug, no USP monograph, not on the 503A bulks list; not eligible for legal pharmacy compounding.

benefits.label: Skin tanning / pigmentation
benefits.detail: Induces melanogenesis and skin darkening via MC1R agonism, confirmed in small human studies.

benefits.label: Erectile / libido effect
benefits.detail: MC4R-mediated erectile activity was observed in early human pilot trials; this effect led to separate development of bremelanotide.

benefits.label: Appetite suppression (preclinical)
benefits.detail: Inhibits food intake in animal models via MC3R/MC4R activity.

risks.label: Melanoma / atypical nevus growth (documented case report)
risks.detail: A published case report documented eruptive atypical nevi and growth of pre-existing nevi in a patient with prior melanoma and dysplastic nevus syndrome after self-administered use; lesions regressed after discontinuation. This is mechanistic evidence that non-selective melanocortin agonism can drive proliferation of neoplastic melanocytes in predisposed individuals.

risks.label: Priapism
risks.detail: Published reports document priapism requiring surgical intervention associated with MT-2 use.

risks.label: Rhabdomyolysis
risks.detail: Published reports associate MT-2 use with rhabdomyolysis.

risks.label: Unregulated product quality
risks.detail: Sold outside any regulated pharmaceutical supply chain; purity, dosing accuracy, and sterility vary widely.

contraindications.label: Personal or family history of melanoma or atypical/dysplastic nevi
contraindications.detail: Documented case evidence of melanocytic proliferation; strong reason to avoid.

contraindications.label: Cardiovascular disease
contraindications.detail: Melanocortin activation can affect cardiovascular tone; caution advised.

interactions.effect: Interactions between melanocortin and opioid systems have been studied preclinically; clinical relevance to MT-2 users is not established.

reconstitution.note: Lyophilized powder reconstituted with bacteriostatic water; concentration depends on diluent volume.

lyophilized.stability: Stable when kept cold and dry.

reconstituted.stability: Refrigerate; use within a limited window.

peptide.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. Melanotan II is not FDA-approved and carries documented, serious safety risks including melanocytic proliferation in susceptible individuals. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide, and see a dermatologist for any new or changing moles.

dose_ranges.context: Commonly cited non-clinical tanning-use range — NOT validated, NOT a recommendation
dose_ranges.note: Frequently reported anecdotal ranges from unregulated/gray-market sources. No regulatory-approved dosing exists for this compound. Given the documented melanoma/nevus safety signal, this range is included strictly for informational and harm-reduction context, not as guidance.

related.note: PT-141 (bremelanotide) is a more selective, FDA-approved melanocortin agonist developed after the erectile effect of the non-selective MT-2 was observed as an incidental finding in early human trials.
